events.title: French National Constituent Assembly Adopts the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
events.description: The National Constituent Assembly of France adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, a foundational document of the French Revolution that set out individual and collective rights, drawing on Enlightenment ideas.
events.significance: It became a cornerstone of modern human rights and democratic thought, influencing constitutions and rights declarations around the world.

events.title: 19th Amendment Certified, Guaranteeing Women's Right to Vote in the United States
events.description: U.S. Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified the ratification of the 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which prohibits denying the right to vote on the basis of sex.
events.significance: The certification culminated decades of suffrage activism and extended voting rights to millions of American women. The date is now commemorated as Women's Equality Day.

events.title: Battle of Crécy
events.description: English forces under King Edward III decisively defeated a larger French army under Philip VI at Crécy in northern France, with English longbowmen playing a key role against French knights and Genoese crossbowmen.
events.significance: The battle was a major English victory early in the Hundred Years' War and demonstrated the power of the longbow, signaling the decline of the traditional mounted feudal knight.

events.title: Albino Luciani Elected Pope John Paul I
events.description: Cardinal Albino Luciani, Patriarch of Venice, was elected pope and took the name John Paul I, the first pope to use a double name. His pontificate lasted only 33 days before his sudden death.
events.significance: His election led to the 'year of three popes' and paved the way for the election of John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in over 400 years.

events.title: Birth of Mother Teresa
events.description: Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu, later known as Mother Teresa, was born in Skopje, then part of the Ottoman Empire. She founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta in 1950 and devoted her life to serving the poor and dying.
events.significance: She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and was canonized by the Catholic Church in 2016, becoming a global symbol of charity and compassion.
